question: Did bounded public GBIF searches and public-web discovery identify site-resolved fish evidence for Yabahan River, Quezon?
purpose: Screen the officially named Yabahan River and Quezon advisory spelling variant Yabahaan for indexed fish occurrences or site-resolved surveys without converting non-retrieval into an absence claim.

gbif.queryTaxonomy: Catalogue of Life Extended Release Actinopterygii
gbif.resultHandling: All four indexed queries returned zero rows. GBIF indexes occurrence metadata; these exact field-term filters do not show that fish are absent, that no survey exists, or that records do not use other locality terms.

queryPhrases: "San Andres, Quezon" fish ichthyofauna river survey
freshwater fish Quezon Province rivers survey San Andres
webSearch.result: No site-resolved fish survey or specimen/occurrence evidence for Yabahan River was identified in this bounded public-web search. Search results included surveys for different waterbodies and unstructured fishing pages, which were not transferred to this river.

findings.evidence: Direct GBIF occurrence API fetches on 2026-11-02 returned zero rows for Philippines plus CoL XR Actinopterygii in four separate indexed searches: locality=Yabahan, locality=Yabahaan, waterBody=Yabahan River, and waterBody=Yabahaan.
supports: only that the four bounded GBIF field-term queries returned zero on 2026-11-02
doesNotSupport: records outside GBIF or indexed under other fields

findings.evidence: DENR DAO 2025-28 names Yabahan River in San Andres, Quezon and lists upstream/downstream monitoring stations with a regulatory B classification. Those stations and the classification are not fish sampling results or a fish checklist.
supports: official waterbody name and locality context

findings.evidence: EMB Table 3.3 lists Yabahan River with San Andres and San Francisco locality context and historical 2020 classification metadata; it is a water-classification table, not fish sampling.
Quezon General Flood Advisory No. 14, issued 7 August 2026, uses the spelling “Yabahaan” as a historical watercourse label. It does not report fish observations.
supports: the advisory spelling variant used for the river-name crosswalk

excludedSearchFindings.title: Diversity and Distribution of Freshwater Fish Assemblages in Tayabas River, Quezon (Philippines)
excludedSearchFindings.reason: A real fish survey was identified, but its sampling sites are on Tayabas River, a different named waterbody; none of its fish records were assigned to Yabahan River.

excludedSearchFindings.title: Freshwater Fishes of Tikub Lake, Tiaong, Quezon, Philippines
excludedSearchFindings.reason: A fish survey for Tikub Lake is a different waterbody; no species were transferred to Yabahan River.

excludedSearchFindings.title: Yabahaan River fishing reports
excludedSearchFindings.reason: The page is a user-generated fishing platform and reports no logged catches; it does not provide biological sampling, voucher evidence, or a fish list.

excludedSearchFindings.title: Giant Lapu-Lapu fish caught in San Andres, Quezon
excludedSearchFindings.reason: The article describes a reported coastal catch near Barangay Inanuran, not a sample from Yabahan River; it is not assigned to this river lead.

nextActions: Keep fish evidence and current presence unknown; do not infer fishlessness from zero results.
Seek dated, station-resolved sampling tables from BFAR IV-A, Quezon LGU, EMB, or university repositories, with methods, identification evidence/vouchers, and reuse terms.
Obtain permitted route-scale hydrography separately before assigning any fish survey station or advisory reach to the Yabahan River route.
nonClaims: This was a bounded discovery screen, not an exhaustive literature, museum-catalog, or occurrence-provider search.
No species, diet, current presence/absence, salinity, water quality, safety, access, fishing rule, river route, or geometry is established.
